learnings.claim: POSIX flock protects processes sharing one checkout, while GitHub Contents API updates require the current blob SHA and serialized remote writes.
learnings.decision: Keep local flock plus atomic replace; remote writers must read the current blob SHA, write serially, and re-read after conflicts.
failure_history: A local file lock cannot coordinate independent GitHub runners or automation branches.
fallback_history: On conflict, fetch the new blob SHA and reassess the delta before one bounded retry.
learnings.next_measurement: Track HTTP 409 or 422 conflicts and verify successful read-back on the merged main branch.
learnings.title: Local and remote write locks are separate

learnings.claim: GitHub Apps should request only the minimum permissions needed; Contents and Workflows permissions are separate capabilities.
learnings.decision: For repository automation, grant Contents only when code/file access is required and add Workflows only when .github/workflows files must be edited.
failure_history: Treating a visible or installed GitHub App as proof of appropriately scoped access can overstate both capability and safety.
fallback_history: If the required permission cannot be confirmed, keep the integration available_unverified and use read-only/manual review instead of expanding access.
learnings.next_measurement: Compare the documented minimum with the actual installed app permissions when authorized account-level visibility is available.
learnings.title: Separate GitHub App Contents and Workflows permissions
